title: Offline Writes, Sync Queues, and Conflict Resolution

scout.purpose: Offline mutation must preserve user intent durably, show an honest optimistic result, and converge with server state after duplicate, reordered, or conflicting delivery.
scout.realWorldUse: Bookmarks, reactions, edits, reading state, and queued uploads may occur across devices while connectivity and processes disappear.
scout.outcome: Persist an outbox operation, apply optimistic local state transactionally, use idempotent synchronization, and choose conflict policy per field.

blocks.text: An optimistic write updates local UI before remote confirmation, but it should first transactionally persist both the desired local state and a pending operation. The outbox row has stable operation ID, entity ID, type, payload or reference, creation order, attempt state, and optional base version. If the process dies, the intent remains. UI can show pending, confirmed, or failed state and offer retry or reversal rather than pretending every local change is already remote.

blocks.caption: The optimistic view and durable operation commit atomically before synchronization.

blocks.title: Write state
rows: At least once with operation ID

sections.title: An outbox makes retry and process death explicit

blocks.text: A synchronizer reads pending operations in a deterministic order, sends an idempotency key, and marks confirmed outcome transactionally. At-least-once delivery means duplicates are expected; server and client operations must be idempotent or deduplicate by operation ID. Coalesce commands only when semantics allow, such as several unsent bookmark toggles becoming final desired state. Preserve destructive or monetary histories. Distinguish transient retry, authentication pause, validation rejection, and permanent conflict.

blocks.caption: The optimistic view and durable operation commit atomically before synchronization.

blocks.title: Optimistic is not imaginary
blocks.text: Persist the intent and its pending status before displaying it as accepted.

sections.title: Conflict policy belongs to domain semantics

blocks.text: Conflict resolution can be server wins, client wins, last-write-wins with trustworthy versioning, field-level merge, set union, operation transform, or user choice. Choose by domain: bookmark desired state may merge by latest version, collaborative text cannot safely use blind timestamps, and deleted server content may invalidate an edit. Store server version or vector metadata required by the contract. Test two devices offline, reordered delivery, duplicate execution, stale base version, logout, and partial batch failure until both sides converge.

Production data work must remain correct after interruption and repetition. Define the source of truth, stable operation identity, transaction boundary, cancellation behaviour, and the state shown before remote confirmation. Exercise empty and stale data, malformed input, duplicate delivery, simultaneous callers, process death, schema upgrade, storage pressure, and connectivity restoration where relevant. Use pure unit tests for mapping and conflict policy, real Room or DataStore instances for persistence contracts, MockWebServer for protocol behaviour, and WorkManager test APIs for durable scheduling. Logs must reveal operation state without exposing tokens, user content, or personal identifiers. A future engineer should be able to explain which component owns every row, cursor, credential, retry, and final user-visible outcome.

inspect.title: Make the optimistic bookmark durable
walkthrough: The UI changes before any durable record of the intent exists.
Navigation or process death cancels the request and loses the bookmark.
Transactionally update Room and an outbox row, then schedule durable synchronization.
inspect.expectedOutput: The bookmark remains pending after restart and eventually confirms or exposes a recoverable rejection.

trap_check.mistake: Using device timestamp for blind last-write-wins across devices.
trap_check.why: Clock skew can make an older edit appear newer.
trap_check.fix: Use server versions or a domain-specific merge contract.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a retry, cache, or abstraction without naming the failure contract.
trap_check.why: The implementation hides ambiguity while duplicate, stale, or lost outcomes remain possible.
trap_check.fix: Write the invariant and an interruption test before introducing machinery.

challenge_intro.task: Implement optimistic bookmark state, durable outbox, idempotent sync, coalescing, authentication pause, conflict versions, rejection recovery, and two-device convergence tests.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Process death never loses accepted intent. Duplicate delivery has one logical effect. Every conflict and permanent rejection has a visible resolution.

recall.prompt: What belongs in the optimistic transaction?
recall.answer: Local desired state and a pending outbox operation.
